Renovation Cost per Sq Ft in Malaysia (2026): Rates by Trade

Published 19 November 2026

In 2026, renovation in Malaysia costs roughly RM40–120 per sq ft for a light refresh, RM90–250 per sq ft for a standard mid-range renovation, and RM170–450+ per sq ft for a premium or full overhaul. A typical 1,000 sq ft condo renovation lands around RM80,000–200,000. Below are the published ranges, the rates by trade behind them, and a worked example that shows how a per-sq-ft figure is built up line by line.

Renovation cost per sq ft: what 2026 guides say

Every source defines its tiers a little differently, which is why the ranges overlap. Here they are side by side:

Source (2026) Light refresh Mid-range Premium / full overhaul
iHome.my RM50–120 RM120–250 RM250–450+
ClickBina RM50–90 RM90–150 RM150–220+ (structural RM180–300+)
Klang Valley report cited by Duotone Studio RM40–70 RM90–160 RM170–300+

What usually separates the tiers:

  • Light refresh: repainting, new flooring over existing tiles, minor repairs, new lights. Little or no hacking.
  • Mid-range: new kitchen and bathrooms, built-in carpentry, plaster ceiling and electrical work.
  • Premium / full overhaul: hacking walls, moving plumbing, premium finishes, extensive custom carpentry, and layout changes on landed homes.

The per-sq-ft figure is based on the built-up area of the home, not just the floor area you work on.

Renovation rates by trade

These are the published 2026 rates that a per-sq-ft figure is made of. Treat them as a reference to check your own rates against, not as prices to copy. Location, access, quantity and material grade all move them.

Trade Typical published rate (2026) Unit
Hacking / demolition RM2,000–3,000 per area (e.g. one bathroom)
Rebuilding walls RM50–80 per sq ft
Waterproofing, bathroom wet works RM1,500–2,000 per bathroom
Tiling labour (tiles not included) RM10–30 per sq ft
Ceramic / porcelain tiles RM11–15 per sq ft
Plaster ceiling RM6–15 per sq ft
Electrical, lighting point RM65–90 per point
Electrical, 13A socket outlet RM100–150 per point
Full rewiring RM3,500–15,000 per home
Interior painting RM1.50–6.80 per sq ft
Kitchen cabinets, melamine RM180–300 per ft run
Kitchen cabinets, plywood RM330–600 per ft run
Built-in wardrobes and other carpentry RM400–900 per ft run

Bathrooms are priced per bathroom more often than per sq ft; see the bathroom renovation quotation guide. Carpentry is usually the biggest single line. It’s priced per foot run, so 20% more cabinet length means roughly 20% more carpentry cost. For more on cabinet pricing, see the kitchen cabinet quotation guide.

Worked example: a 1,000 sq ft condo, built up line by line

Here’s how a mid-range scope adds up for a 1,000 sq ft condo: new floor tiles throughout, two bathrooms and the kitchen redone, plaster ceiling in the living areas, kitchen cabinets and two wardrobes. The quantities and rates are illustrative, picked from within the published ranges above.

Item Unit Qty Rate (RM) Amount (RM)
Floor & lift protection, renovation permit handling lot 1 1,500.00 1,500.00
Hack kitchen & 2 bathrooms, incl. disposal area 3 2,500.00 7,500.00
Waterproofing, 2 bathrooms bathroom 2 1,800.00 3,600.00
Supply & lay 600 × 600mm floor tiles sq ft 900 25.00 22,500.00
Supply & lay wall tiles, kitchen & bathrooms sq ft 400 25.00 10,000.00
Flat plaster ceiling with cornice sq ft 600 8.00 4,800.00
Lighting points point 20 80.00 1,600.00
13A socket outlets point 10 120.00 1,200.00
Water points, concealed piping point 6 350.00 2,100.00
Kitchen base cabinets, laminated plywood ft run 10 380.00 3,800.00
Kitchen wall cabinets, laminated plywood ft run 10 330.00 3,300.00
Wardrobes, 2 bedrooms ft run 16 450.00 7,200.00
Repaint walls & ceilings, 2 coats sq ft 3,000 2.50 7,500.00
Final cleaning & debris removal lot 1 800.00 800.00
Total 77,400.00

That’s RM77 per sq ft, at the low end of mid-range. And it doesn’t yet include the kitchen countertop, sanitary fittings, light fittings or a contingency, which homeowner guides suggest setting at 10–15%. Add those and the job moves well into the RM90–120 per sq ft band. This is why a per-sq-ft quote made on the spot so often goes wrong.

How contractors should use per-sq-ft figures

  • As a sanity check, not a price. Build the quotation by trade, then divide the total by the built-up area. If the result is far below the range for that scope, look for missing lines.
  • Itemise every line. Unit, quantity and rate on each line lets you re-measure fairly and price changes consistently. A lump sum invites arguments, and homeowner guides warn against quotes with no breakdown.
  • List the exclusions. Countertops, sanitary ware, light fittings, appliances and management deposits are the usual gaps between what the client thinks is included and what is.
  • Watch markup vs margin. A 30% markup on cost is only a 23% margin. The markup vs margin guide has conversion tables.

Frequently asked questions

How much does renovation cost per sq ft in Malaysia in 2026?
Published 2026 guides put a light refresh at roughly RM40 to RM120 per sq ft, a standard mid-range renovation at roughly RM90 to RM250 per sq ft, and a full or premium overhaul from about RM170 to RM450 or more per sq ft. The ranges overlap because each source defines the tiers differently.
How much does it cost to renovate a 1,000 sq ft condo in Malaysia?
Roughly RM80,000 to RM200,000 for a typical renovation, according to 2026 guides. A cosmetic refresh can cost much less, and a premium job with full custom carpentry can cost more. The scope of carpentry, wet works and hacking decides where a job lands.
Should a contractor quote renovation per sq ft?
Use the per-sq-ft figure only as a sanity check. Quote by trade, with a unit, quantity and rate on every line. A single per-sq-ft price hides what is included, which leads to disputes, and makes it hard to price changes fairly later.
What is a foot run?
A foot run (ft run) is one foot of length measured along the wall. Kitchen cabinets, wardrobes and other built-in carpentry are priced per foot run, not per square foot.
